entries.notes: SAL is a DIRECT source geography for G01/G02/G35 (ABS publishes these tables natively at SAL) — no ASGS correspondence weighting is needed or used for this dataset; direct_or_derived='direct' for every row. This matters especially for G02's medians, which cannot be validly re-derived from a finer geography via correspondence weighting (median of medians is not a valid statistic) — reading them directly from the native SAL file is the only correct approach.

entries.dataset_name: 2021 Census GCP DataPack — POA for AUS (short header), tables G01/G02/G35
entries.variable_codes: identical to the SAL entry above — same G01/G02/G35 column set, POA_CODE_2021 keyed
entries.notes: Same direct-geography note as SAL — POA is a native GCP DataPack geography for these tables.

entries.geography_level: SAL/POA (2016 boundaries — ASGS Edition 1, NOT the ASGS Edition 3 (2021) boundaries this warehouse's geography backbone is built on)
entries.notes: SCOPE DECISION (documented per the task's own hedge 'where directly supportable'): 2016 Census SAL/POA boundaries do not align 1:1 with the 2021 SAL/POA boundaries already loaded into core.dim_geography (ASGS Ed.3 2021). Producing a valid population_2016 figure on today's 2021-boundary geography backbone would require a full SA1-level 2016-to-2021 boundary correspondence exercise — comparable in scope to a dedicated mini-sprint, not a same-sprint addition alongside four other new capabilities. Rather than approximate with a mismatched boundary join (which would violate this sprint's 'do not invent geography relationships' rule), population_2016 and population_growth_2016_2021_pct are left NULL in mart.suburb_demographic_profile_2021 / mart.postcode_demographic_profile_2021 for every row, with data_quality_status noting the reason. population (2021 only) and median_age are populated from the current, correctly-aligned 2021 data.
